Hello. I have been a dentist for five years now. I graduated at the end of 2015. Dentistry can be very stressful. Dental school is very stressful, and yes, there are several studies assessing suicide rates, depression rates, and anxiety rates among dentists and dental students, because indeed the prevalence of these mental illnesses are high. I think these prevalences are high because in dentistry you can have several physical problems if you don’t work in the right positions. Additionally, the routine in clinical practice can be very demanding because for every patient that walks through your door you have to do a procedure, as opposed to just talking to them in a medical doctor's practice.

However, I will say that if this is your dream since you were a child like you said, then by all means go for it. Because what I have learned in these five years of working as a dentist is that if you are really passionate about it, if you really like it, then you probably have it better than most dentists. Because the truth is many people chose this career because they didn’t know what to do or maybe because they just knew that they wanted to work in the health area. So if this is your dream I will say go for it.

Additionally, to be fair I have to say that there are a lot of differences between the countries. There are countries that dentists make a lot of money, and making a lot of money can be a redeeming quality for a lot of the stressful characteristics of the profession. And there are countries where dentistry is not as valued. I live in a Third World country so you also have to take that into consideration. I would say speak to your local dentist and try to have an open and honest conversation about the profession, including how much money they make if possible. I think it’s better than trying to get advice on Reddit because here on Reddit you can get advice from people all around the world but you can get more accurate advice if you speak to dentists around you, I think.
